Most of the crypto faculty (Persichetti, Bai, Das, Kuchta, Sica) are in Mathematics and Statistics, not EECS; an EECS MS thesis must be chaired by EECS graduate faculty, so Azarderakhsh is the in-department crypto advisor. Azarderakhsh is PQC hardware/engineering and has 0 core-venue or crypto-themed CCS/USENIX/S&P papers in 2021-25 (he publishes in IEEE TVLSI/TCAD/TCAS, CT-RSA, HOST, ePrint). Theory-side lattice work: Bai (lattice reduction, quantum algorithms), Das (lattice/knapsack hardness), Kuchta (lattice ZK).
notes: Faculty: CSrankings lists only Azarderakhsh and Nojoumian as FAU crypto/security names; the math-department cryptographers were added from the CCIS faculty/research pages and their directory or homepages. Excluded: Mehrdad Nojoumian (EECS; 2021-26 dblp titles are mostly autonomous-vehicle trust and blockchain reputation, one PQC side-channel survey), Feng-Hao Liu (moved to Washington State University, Aug 2023), Koray Karabina (not on the CCIS faculty or research lists; a 2025 Carleton thesis board lists him at "National Research Center"). Topics come from the fixed tag regex over all 2021-26 dblp titles ("post-quantum" not counted as quantum crypto), since most of these people publish outside the counted venues. Counts include CHES/TCHES per this pass, unlike the original dataset method, which counted CRYPTO/EUROCRYPT/ASIACRYPT/TCC/PKC/JoC only. Persichetti is the only one with a TCHES paper in the window (LESS is Even More, 2025), so he has 3 papers without it. Length null: the MS CS catalog gives no time to degree. research_fit_note: 30-credit MS with a thesis option (9 thesis credits, CIS 6971; thesis defense replaces the comprehensive exam). The catalog says the thesis track prepares students for doctoral study. A USF CSE-related MS can count toward the PhD as post-master's status (42 instead of 72 credits). Crypto in Bellini is applied: Yavuz (PQ/IoT signatures, secure logging), Mozaffari Kermani (PQC hardware and fault detection). Neither has a core-venue paper in 2021-25. Yavuz's ORAM and searchable-encryption work (S3ORAM CCS 2017; Efficient Oblivious Data Structures, IEEE TCC 2021) falls before the window or gives only one recent title, so ORAM is not tagged. The theory side is Biasse in Mathematics (isogeny/SCALLOP, quantum cryptanalysis, code equivalence).
notes: Faculty: CSrankings lists Yavuz and Mozaffari Kermani; Biasse (Mathematics) and Behnia (School of Information Systems, USF) were added from usf-crypto.org/people.html. Excluded: Giacomo Micheli (Mathematics, Core Faculty; 2021-26 dblp is mostly coding theory and finite fields, with only 2 crypto-adjacent titles), Tefjol Pllaha (Mathematics; quantum PIR capacity and QLDPC coding theory, information theory rather than cryptography), and other affiliated faculty (Karam, Koelsch, Savchuk and others) with no crypto publication record checked. Counts include CHES/TCHES per this pass; none of the USF people has a CHES/TCHES paper in the window. Yavuz's S&P 2026 PQC-PKI paper is outside the 2021-25 window, and the 'QRSec 2025' CCS entry is a workshop summary, so it is excluded. The S&P 2025 privacy-preserving federated learning paper (Yavuz, Kermani, Behnia) does not match the crypto-title test. Topics come from the fixed tag regex over all 2021-26 dblp titles ("post-quantum" not counted as quantum crypto). Length null: no official time to degree. GRE: Sahmoud (domestic, UC Davis BS, an R1 university) qualifies for the exemption.
